title: Early detection of side effects in patients with metastatic melanoma receiving immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy by investigation of the CD8+ immune infiltrate using [89Zr]Zr-Df-IAB22M2C-PET
summary:
Since 40-80% of patients with metastatic melanoma do not respond to so-called immune-checkpoint inhibitor therapy (ICT) with therapeutic antibodies and many of these patients show rapid progression. Thus, it is of enormous clinical importance to identify patients who may not benefit from ICT or suffer from immune-mediated side effects at the earliest possible stage. 
An early change of the therapy to a more promising alternative could not only further reduce the mortality in this patient population, but also significantly reduce the immense costs of these therapies for the healthcare system. To date, ICT in metastatic melanoma has been administered according to clinical indication and adjusted or discontinued in the event of progression or severe side effects. 
In this context, factors such as certain blood count constellations, patient age, and previous diseases may increase the likelihood of treatment failure or severe side effects, but there is a lack of reliable biomarker or specific test.
CD8-specific positron emission tomography (PET) imaging provides a specific tool to visualize the relevant CD8+ T cells which mediate both the anti-tumorigenic immune response and the adverse inflammatory side effects. Therefore, we aim to investigate to what extent the distribution of CD8+ T cells as assessed by means of [89Zr]Zr-Df-IAB22M2C PET (CD8-directed PET) allows an early detection or even a prediction of potential side effects related to the therapeutic response and to compare with standard of care imaging.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients must meet all the following criteria:
• Male or female patients ≥18 years of age at the time of signing the informed consent
• Patients with metastasized or irresectable melanoma stage III/IV 
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance (ECOG) Status ≤ 2
• Patients scheduled for ICT by tumor board decision
• Understand and voluntarily sign an informed consent document prior to any study related assessments/ procedures.
• Able to adhere to the study visit schedule and other protocol requirements
• Consent to practice double-barrier contraception until end of the study (28 days after last [89Zr]Zr-Df-IAB22M2C injection)
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if one or more of the following criteria are met:
• Known hypersensitivity to [89Zr]Zr-Df-IAB22M2C or its components or to any drug with similar chemical structure or to any excipient present in the pharmaceutical form of the investigational medicinal product.
• Clinical signs of active infection (>Grade 2 according to CTCAE version 5.0).
• Major surgery within 4 weeks of starting study treatment. Patients must have recovered from any effects of major surgery.
• Heart failure NYHA III/IV.
• Patients not able to declare meaningful informed consent on their own.
• Women during pregnancy and lactation; female patients of childbearing potential or male patients with female partners of childbearing potential not willing to practice effective contraception by using a double-barrier method from Day 0 until 28 days post-dose.
• Male patients planning to donate sperm while participating in the study and for at least 28 days after end of study treatment.
• Participation in other clinical trials or observation period of competing trials.
